snippet:
📆 MONTHLY MOMENTUM STRATEGY (ETF SECTOR ROTATION STRATEGY IN EEM, SPY, AND TLT) 🔄📈🌍

In this post, we give an example of a very easy and simple ETF rotation strategy among SPY (S&P 500), TLT (Treasury bonds), and EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets) that has worked pretty well over the last two decades. It has beaten “buy and hold” with lower drawdowns. That was until 2022, which was a very bad year for the strategy.

We backtest the following trading rules:

➨ It's based on monthly quotes in the ETFs SPY, EEM, and TLT.
➨ Every month rank them based on last month's performance and go long the best performing ETF.
➨ Hold for one month and repeat (or continue being long the same instrument).

Without slippage and taxes the equity curves look like the image shown below.

Can the strategy be improved or made different? If you have any suggestions, please comment 👇

snippet:
MONTHLY MOMENTUM STRATEGY 🔄 (ETF SECTOR ROTATION IN EEM, SPY, AND TLT)

In this post, we give an example of a very easy and simple ETF rotation strategy among SPY (S&P 500), TLT (Treasury bonds), and EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets) that has worked pretty well over the last two decades. It has beaten “buy and hold” with lower drawdowns. That was until 2022, which was a very bad year for the strategy.

The theory held up pretty well in the backtest we did over two decades. We backtest the following trading rules:

➨ It's based on monthly quotes in the ETFs SPY, EEM, and TLT.
➨ Every month rank them based on last month's performance and go long the best performing ETF.
➨ Hold for one month and repeat (or continue being long the same instrument).

This is all there is to it. It can hardly get any simpler than that. Obviously, this strategy is best performed in a tax-deferred account because of the frequent rotation among the ETFs.

title: WEEKLY TRADING STRATEGY – BACKTEST WITH WEEKLY CHARTS, RETURNS, AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS 📉📅
snippet:
WEEKLY TRADING STRATEGY – BACKTEST WITH WEEKLY CHARTS, RETURNS, AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS 📉📅

The weekly trading strategy is a method of trading that focuses on the weekly price action. This can take any form: It could be positional trading based on the price action on the weekly chart or using the weekly chart to get a broader view of the market for a trend-following system on the daily chart, or even a weekly rotation system. It could also be a weekly swing trading strategy that focuses on capturing the price movement of the weekly price bars.

We backtest the following trading rules:

➨ Every Friday at the close we rank the ETFs based on one single variable.
➨ Buy the one ranked the lowest. 
➨ Hold for one week and rinse and repeat.

The equity curve of the strategy looks like the image shown below.

Can the strategy be improved or made different? If you have any suggestions, please comment 👇

title: 🇬🇧 LONDON BREAKOUT STRATEGY: RULES AND BACKTEST PERFORMANCE 📈
snippet:
🇬🇧 LONDON BREAKOUT STRATEGY: RULES AND BACKTEST PERFORMANCE 📈

Also known as the London daybreak strategy, the London breakout strategy is a day trading strategy that seeks to trade the upward or downward breakout of the day’s trading range that’s formed before the opening of the London session. This breakout usually happens within the first three hours into the London session. if the breakout is to the upside, traders take long positions, and if it is to the downside, traders take short positions.

We backtest the following trading rules:

➨ We use the high and low from 0300 to 0800 London time to determine the high and low (resistance and support).
➨ When the price breaks above the high, we go long (between 0800 and 1100 London time).
➨ When the price breaks below the low, we go long (between 0800 and 1100 London time).
➨ We use a time exit (no stops or profit targets) at 1200, 1300, 1400, 1500, 1600, and 1700 London time.

Let’s look (Image below) at the results for the different time stops when we enter long on a breakout above the high.

Can the strategy be improved or made different? If you have any suggestions, please comment 👇

title: ETF Outflows: Bitcoin’s Local Low Lifeline
snippet:
ETF Outflows: Bitcoin’s Local Low Lifeline

Bitcoin’s spot ETFs — the $35 billion institutional backbone that has defined this cycle since their January 2024 debut — are flashing their first major net outflows in months. The 7-day moving average slipped to -2,000 BTC in late October 2025, marking the sharpest weekly bleed since May. Historically, these red bars have clustered around local market bottoms, where weak hands exit and conviction quietly reloads.

Amid Uptober’s -2.32% close, $2.1 billion in long liquidations, and long-term holders offloading 1.13 million BTC over the year, this outflow isn’t collapse — it’s calibration. As takers snapped up $364 million in BTC during dips and whales net-added 50,000 BTC in October, the ETF drain reads more as a cleansing reset than structural rejection.

If history rhymes — and it often does — the turn from outflows to inflows could again mark the spark of Moonvember, where BTC’s +46% historical November average finds fresh footing on the ashes of exhaustion.

Outflow Anatomy: From Mania to Maturity

ETF flow data reveals a cycle of expansion, fatigue, and flush:

Q1 2025: Mania. Green bars peaked at +8,000 BTC/week in March as BlackRock’s IBIT and Fidelity’s FBTC hoovered $20B combined, netting 200,000 BTC in the quarter.

Q2: Momentum. Flows averaged +4,000 BTC/week through halving hype, buttressed by treasuries’ $800B BTC accumulation.
